name: Tawas Point Lighthouse
story: A moving shoreline left this beacon inland twice. Look for the difference between the historic tower and the modern navigation light.
access: Short approach from parking; the tower has 85 steps. Park entry and lighthouse admission are separate.

name: Au Sable Light Station
story: A light, fog signal and keepers’ homes tell the story of navigation along the Shipwreck Coast.
access: Walk 1.5 miles each way from Hurricane River day-use parking. No bicycles on the access road. Secure shoes required for tower climbs.

name: Split Rock Lighthouse
story: The cliff gives this short tower its commanding view. Separate the lighthouse building visit from the state park shoreline viewpoint.
access: Historic-site admission and state park vehicle permits cover different experiences. Check MNHS hours before booking.

name: Big Sable Point Lighthouse
story: A long approach through dunes is part of the experience; leave enough daylight for the return walk.
access: About 1.8 miles each way on the sand-and-gravel lighthouse path in Ludington State Park. Verify tower hours with Lakeshore Keepers.

name: St. Joseph North Pier Lights
story: Two lights and an elevated catwalk trace the harbor entrance. The beach offers a way to study the structures without walking the pier.
access: North pier access is through Tiscornia Beach. Wet, icy or wave-washed piers require a different plan; use a land viewpoint.

name: Old Mackinac Point Lighthouse
story: At the narrow meeting of two lakes, a keeper had to distinguish a safe passage from a dangerous shore.
access: Mainland historic site in Mackinaw City. Tower entry follows the operator’s tour rules and seasonal schedule.

name: Fort Gratiot Lighthouse
story: Michigan’s oldest surviving lighthouse marks the transition from Lake Huron into the St. Clair River.
access: Check Port Huron Museums for guided tower tours. County park grounds access does not promise tower admission.

name: Port Austin Reef Light
story: A reef light stands where navigation turns between Lake Huron and Saginaw Bay. Getting there is a boat trip, not a drive.
access: Approximately 2.5 miles offshore. Tours require an operator reservation and suitable marine conditions. Do not navigate using this map.

name: Point Clark Lighthouse
story: This limestone tower belongs to the Imperial lighthouse system that helped open Lake Huron and Georgian Bay to shipping.
access: Verify tower tour dates and admission with the site operator; grounds and tower access differ.

name: Marblehead Lighthouse
story: Ohio DNR identifies Marblehead as the oldest lighthouse in continuous operation on the Great Lakes.
access: Visit the state park grounds; tower climbs follow a separate seasonal schedule. Rocky shorelines can be slippery.

name: Charlotte–Genesee Lighthouse
story: The historic tower now stands inland from the lake: a chance to read the changing relationship between a harbor and its shore.
access: Check the historical society’s posted tour hours. Group visits require advance arrangements.

name: Thirty Mile Point Lighthouse
story: A beacon on Lake Ontario’s south shore warns of shoals near Golden Hill. Connect the building’s story to the lake beyond it.
access: Located in Golden Hill State Park; check park entry requirements and current lighthouse tours.

name: Tibbetts Point Lighthouse
story: Where Lake Ontario meets the St. Lawrence River, an operating light still marks the passage.
access: Grounds and selected buildings can be visited according to operator hours; the active lighthouse tower is not accessible to visitors.
